To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the essential oil of thyme and oregano were the most potent antimicrobials, with MICs of 0*03-0*06% and 0*03%, respectively.
the antimicrobial activity of 52 plant oils was determined using a standard method, and 20 of the oils were also investigated by a second method.
the essential oils of oregano and lemongrass were the most active of the oils tested, and the essential oils of apricot kernel, pumpkin and sweet almond were inactive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the antimicrobial properties of plant extracts and essential oils.
the identification and development of natural products that are effective against microorganisms of medical and industrial importance.
the identification of the antimicrobial activity of a wide range of plant extracts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
plant essential oils are effective antimicrobial agents, but their activity depends on the oil and the organism.

the antimicrobial activity of essential oil is highly dependent upon its chemical composition and that there is a wide variation in the antimicrobial activity between different oils of the same plant and even between different samples of the same oil.
the antimicrobial activity of essential oil and extracts is dependent on the organism tested, the method of testing, the concentration of essential oil or extract and the oil or extract tested.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the essential oils of lemongrass, oregon, bay and thyme, as well as the essential oils of cinnamon, clove, tea tree, eucalyptus, rosemary, peppermint, lavender, lemon myrtle, niaouli and wintergreen, and the extracts of cinnamon bark, clove bud, oregano, bay leaves and lemongrass have the potential to be used as antimicrobial preservatives in pharmaceutical and food products.

the essential oils and plant extracts tested have a potential to be used as natural preservatives in the food, pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and agricultural industry, but also in the health sector for treating and preventing infectious diseases.
the essential oils of thyme, lemongrass and oregano were most active against the bacteria, fungi and yeasts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
essential oils are a good source of natural antimicrobial compounds.
essential oils are a rich source of antimicrobial substances that can be used in a number of ways to combat bacterial infections.
essential oils and extracts are not a panacea for antimicrobial activity.
